title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 2.4 Samson kills a Lion

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Judges 14:5-9 tells how the Spirit of the LORD came upon Samson so that he tore a young lion apart with his bare hands. In this sub-strand you will retell that short story, acknowledge God's power, and learn to trust God when you face hard things.

## Strand 2.0: The Holy Bible
Sub-strand 2.4: Samson kills a Lion
Suggested lessons: 2

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) retell the story of Samson; Judges 14: 5- 9
b) acknowledge God’s power in his or her life
c) trust in God to cope with the challenges of life

## Key inquiry questions
1. How does the story of Samson portray God’s power?

## Core competencies
• Imagination and Creativity: the skill of originality is nurtured as learners model a lion and compose a poem.
• Communication: the skill of speaking clearly and effectively is exhibited as they read in turns.

## Values
• Respect: learners take turns to read the Bible and listen to each other’s ideas.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Social Cohesion: learners portray teamwork as they role-play the story of, ‘Samson kills a Lion.’

## Links to other learning areas
• English: reading and writing skills are applied as learners read and compose a poem.
• Creative Arts: learners draw, colour and model a lion.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 2.0 The Holy Bible, Sub-strand 2.4 Samson kills a Lion
• Judges 14:5-9

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: The story in Judges 14:5-9

LESSON 1: THE STORY IN JUDGES 14:5-9
====================================

## What you will learn
• Retell Judges 14:5-9 in order.
• Say what the Spirit of the LORD enabled Samson to do.

Curriculum outcomes: a) retell the story of Samson; Judges 14: 5- 9

## Introduction
A lion is strong. A person does not tear a lion apart with bare hands. Judges 14:5-9 says Samson did, because the Spirit of the LORD came upon him.

## Notes
Read Judges 14:5-9 in turns. The story is short. Keep every detail inside these verses.

### On the way to Timnah
Samson went down to Timnah with his father and mother. As they came near the vineyards of Timnah, a young lion came roaring toward him.

### What Samson did
The Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon Samson. He tore the lion apart with his bare hands, as one might tear a young goat. He did not tell his father or his mother what he had done. Then he went on and talked with the woman, and he liked her.

### The honey
Some time later Samson went back to marry her. He turned aside to look at the lion's carcass. In it was a swarm of bees and some honey. He scooped the honey out with his hands and ate it as he walked. When he rejoined his parents he gave them some, and they ate it too. He did not tell them that he had taken the honey from the lion's carcass.

### Retelling without adding
Say only this: the journey with his parents, the roaring lion, the Spirit of the LORD, the tearing with bare hands, the secret he kept, the later visit, the bees and the honey, and the honey he shared without explaining where it came from. Do not bring in other Samson stories that are not in these verses.

Draw or model a lion so that you remember the animal in the story. Compose a short poem that follows the same events: the road, the roar, God's Spirit, and the honey. A poem is a way of retelling, not a place to invent new events.

## Key words
• Spirit of the LORD — God's Spirit, who came upon Samson with power
• carcass — the dead body of the lion
• bare hands — hands with no weapon

## Activity: Read, draw and compose
You will need: Bible, Paper, Clay or pencils, Colours
1. In turns, read Judges 14:5-9.
2. Model a lion with clay, or draw and colour a lion.
3. Draw a picture of Samson killing the lion.
4. Compose a short poem titled "Samson kills a lion" using only the events in the passage.
5. If a video clip about Samson is available, watch the part that matches this story and say which details are in Judges 14:5-9.

## Practice
1. Where was Samson going when the lion met him, and who was with him?
2. How was Samson able to tear the lion apart?
3. What did Samson later find in the lion's carcass?

## Summary
• A young lion roared at Samson near the vineyards of Timnah.
• The Spirit of the LORD enabled him to tear it apart with his bare hands.
• Later he found honey in the carcass and shared it without saying where it came from.

### Answers to practice
1. He was going to Timnah with his father and mother.
2. The Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him, and he tore it with his bare hands.
3. A swarm of bees and some honey. He ate some and gave some to his parents, but he did not tell them where it came from.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: God's power and trusting Him

LESSON 2: GOD'S POWER AND TRUSTING HIM
======================================

## What you will learn
• Acknowledge God's power in his or her life.
• Trust God when facing challenges.

Curriculum outcomes: b) acknowledge God’s power in his or her life; c) trust in God to cope with the challenges of life

## Introduction
Samson did not win because his hands were ordinary hands. God's Spirit gave the power. The same God is strong enough for the hard things in a child's life.

## Notes
Judges 14:6 is the centre of the lesson. The Spirit of the LORD came upon Samson, and only then did the lion fall. The story portrays God's power, not a lesson in fighting animals. Children must not go near wild animals or try to copy Samson's act. The lion was a real danger, and God is the one who gave the strength.

### Acknowledging God's power
To acknowledge is to admit openly. You acknowledge God's power when you say:

- God is stronger than any danger.
- The strength people have is a gift from Him.
- He can help when you are afraid, sick, or in trouble.
- Praise belongs to Him, as the people in other Bible stories praised God for His mighty acts.

Samson kept the event secret from his parents. We do not copy the secret. We thank God openly for His help.

### Trusting God with challenges
A challenge is a hard thing you cannot easily solve. Grade 4 challenges may include a difficult subject, sickness at home, a quarrel, or fear on the way to school. Trusting God means you depend on Him while you also do what is wise.

- Pray and tell Him the problem.
- Obey the safety rules of your parents. Do not approach dangerous animals.
- Ask a trusted person for help.
- Keep doing your duty, as Samson continued on the road God had given him that day.
- Sing about God's power so that fear does not have the last word.

God's power in Samson's hands teaches you that you are not alone in a hard moment. You may not tear a lion apart. You can still trust the God who is able.

## Key words
• power — God's ability to do what people cannot do by themselves
• acknowledge — to admit and say openly that something is true
• challenge — a hard situation that needs help and courage

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A learner says, "I will fight any danger alone, like Samson." What is the right lesson from Judges 14:6?

Working:
1. Samson did not win by ordinary strength.
2. The Spirit of the LORD came upon him.
3. Children should not copy the fight. They should trust God's power and stay safe.

Answer: The story shows God's power, not a plan for children to fight lions or other dangers alone.

## Activity: Sing of God's power
You will need: Bible, Exercise book
1. Read Judges 14:6 again and say who gave Samson the power.
2. List challenges learners face and write one sentence of trust beside each.
3. Sing a song on God's power.
4. Each learner says, "I acknowledge God's power in my life," and gives one example of depending on Him.

## Practice
1. Who gave Samson the power to kill the lion?
2. Should children try to fight wild animals because of this story? Why?
3. Give one way to trust God when you face a challenge.

## Summary
• The Spirit of the LORD gave Samson the power.
• We acknowledge that power and do not try to copy the fight.
• Trust God in your own challenges by praying and doing what is wise.

### Answers to practice
1. God, by the Spirit of the LORD.
2. No. The story shows God's power. Children should stay away from wild animals and trust God while obeying safety rules.
3. Any one: pray, obey safety rules, tell a trusted person, keep doing your duty, sing of God's power.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 2.4 SAMSON KILLS A LION
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which verses tell how Samson killed a lion?
   A. Judges 14:5-9
   B. Luke 19:2-10
   C. Genesis 41:14-24
   D. Numbers 22:28

2. Who was with Samson on the way to Timnah?
   A. His father and mother
   B. Balak and Balaam
   C. The twelve disciples
   D. Pharaoh

3. The young lion came...
   A. roaring toward him
   B. sleeping in the house
   C. already dead on the road
   D. carrying honey in its mouth

4. Samson tore the lion apart...
   A. with a sword his mother gave him
   B. with his bare hands
   C. by calling the army
   D. with a net

5. What did he find in the carcass later?

6. Did Samson tell his parents that he had killed the lion?
   A. Yes, at once
   B. No, he told neither his father nor his mother
   C. He told only the town
   D. He wrote it on a scroll that day

7. The power in the story came from...
   A. Samson's weapon
   B. the Spirit of the LORD
   C. the bees
   D. the crowd

8. How should a learner acknowledge God's power?

9. When you face a challenge you should...
   A. fight every danger alone to copy Samson
   B. trust God, pray, and do what is wise and safe
   C. hide and refuse all help
   D. go near wild animals to test God

10. Why must children not try to kill a lion like Samson?
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 2.4 SAMSON KILLS A LION
========================================

1. A. Judges 14:5-9
   The sub-strand reads Judges 14:5-9.

2. A. His father and mother
   Judges 14:5 says he went with his father and mother.

3. A. roaring toward him
   The lion came roaring toward Samson near the vineyards.

4. B. with his bare hands
   Judges 14:6 says he tore it apart with his bare hands.

5. A swarm of bees and some honey.
   Judges 14:8-9 records the bees, the honey, and the sharing with his parents.

6. B. No, he told neither his father nor his mother
   Judges 14:6 says he told neither his father nor his mother.

7. B. the Spirit of the LORD
   God's Spirit came upon Samson. That is God's power.

8. By saying openly that God is stronger than any danger and by thanking Him for help.
   Acknowledging means admitting God's power in words and thanks.

9. B. trust God, pray, and do what is wise and safe
   Trust in God includes prayer and wise safety, not copying the killing of the lion.

10. Because Samson acted only when the Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and children must stay away from wild animals.
   The story portrays God's power, not a method for children to copy.
